title: The Chair of Saint Peter (22 February)
hookLine: a feast of Peter's teaching office, not a piece of furniture

lines: THE FAR END OF SAINT PETER'S.
cards: Walk to the far end of Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome, past the great canopy over the altar, and look up.

Floating in a burst of gilded rays, held up by four giant bronze figures, is a chair: a huge, ornate bronze throne by the sculptor Bernini. Tourists photograph it and ask, is that where the pope sits? It isn't.
And the feast on February 22 isn't really about a chair either. It's about a word that gave us cathedral.

teach.b: In the ancient world, a teacher sat to teach. The chair, in Greek and Latin cathedra, was the sign of authority to teach, and a bishop's church is called a cathedral because his chair is in it.
So this is a feast of a role, not of furniture: Peter's office of teaching and holding the Church together, which Catholics believe continues in the bishop of Rome. The gospel is Matthew 16.

teach.h: WHO DO YOU SAY I AM?
teach.b: Jesus asks his disciples, who do people say I am? Then, who do you say I am? Simon answers: Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God.
And Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "That thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it." It's a pun.
Peter's new name, Petros in Greek, Kepha in Aramaic, means rock.
Christians read this verse differently, and fairly. Catholics see Peter's office as the rock, handed on to his successors.
Orthodox Christians honor Peter as first among the apostles but understand that primacy differently. Many Protestants read the rock as Peter's confession of faith, or as Christ himself.
Inside Bernini's bronze chair is an older wooden one, long honored as Peter's, though it comes from centuries after him.

teach.h: UPON THIS ROCK I WILL BUILD MY CHURCH.
teach.b: The Church once kept two feasts of Peter's chair, one for Rome and one for Antioch, where tradition says he led the church first; they were combined on this day.
And remember who got the name: the same man who would deny knowing Jesus three times. The rock was a man who cracked, and was forgiven.

how: Catholics keep February 22 as the feast of the Chair of Saint Peter, praying for the pope; in Saint Peter's Basilica the altar of the Chair is decorated with candles for the day.

games.q: Jesus asks his disciples: who do you say I am? you're Simon. what do you answer?
o: thou art Christ, the Son of the living God.
games.why: Simon says it, and Jesus gives him a new name: thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.

practice: Catholics pray for the pope today, and if you pray, you can too: for his health, his judgment, his peace.

If you don't, choose anyone who has to hold a group together, a parent, a principal, a team lead, a pastor, and sit with what it's like to be the rock others lean on and still a person who can crack. Wish them strength.

wordCard.voice: Cathedra, the chair. The ancient sign of a teacher's authority, the word behind cathedral, and the reason this feast of Peter's office isn't about furniture. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: Peter, and rock; the wordplay of Matthew 16:18.
